artifacts.summary: Settles store consolidation (reuse issues.jsonl, correct error-handling.md's stale errors.json pointer), a new infra/transport-unavailable class, a general occurrence-based collapse rule via the existing tags seam, honest per-class capture-point mechanics (mechanical for sapience-retrieve.sh/sapience-remember.sh, agent-cooperation-dependent for MCP tool failures), the no-task-context fallback to events.jsonl, a push-based central log design, and explicit boundary statements against tasks 477, 484, 519, 543, and 562.

memory_candidates.content: In this agent-system, the issue-log's `tags` field (open object, documented in issue-log.md's 'The tags Seam' section) is the designed extension point for adding structured per-entry metadata (e.g. an occurrence count with first_seen/last_seen for collapsing repeated same-class entries) without any schema or script change to issue-record.sh. Reach for this seam before proposing a new field or a new store.

orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's --aggregate already performs group_by(.class) cross-task/cross-entry collapse into one proposal per class with a citations list, and already reads null/omitted resolution as open (reporting implicit_open_count). Before proposing a new aggregation or classification mechanism against a 'signal destroyed by repetition' complaint, read this script directly -- the report-layer grouping frequently already exists; the real cost is usually write volume or an unbounded citations list, not an ungrouped report.

This repo's merged Claude Code settings (settings-hooks.json) carry no wildcard-matcher PostToolUse hook -- the only PostToolUse entry matches Write only, for a specs/state.json validator. There is therefore no mechanical, repo-side way to intercept an arbitrary MCP tool call's failure (e.g. a Sapience 503 surfaced via ~/.sapience/mcp.py, which is vendor-owned and outside the repo). Any error class whose only visibility is an MCP tool-call error in the transcript is agent-cooperation-dependent, not mechanically capturable, absent a new hook (itself usually out of scope under a 'no new hook' cost ceiling).
